page: Vultr vc2-6c-16gb is a Cloud Compute virtual server featuring 6 shared vCPUs mapped from 3 physical Intel Xeon cores on the x86_64 architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the processor includes a cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 4 MB L2, and 16 MB L3. The system is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 2.67 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 320 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate multi-core capabilities alongside weaker single-core metrics. The stress-ng multi-core test achieved a score of 6774.42, placing it in the average tier, whereas the single-core score of 1272.09 is classified as weak. Memory read bandwidth is average, reaching 407.68 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 48.31 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks, though large block write bandwidth drops to a weak 18.72 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks show limitations, with a weak Passmark encryption score of 1705.87 and poor single-threaded gzip compression performance of 18.3 GB/sec. However, the server demonstrates average efficiency in Redis SET operations, processing 6.15 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the vc2-6c-16gb offers a high density of vCPUs and NVMe storage for budget-conscious deployments, though this is balanced against the shared CPU allocation which can introduce performance variability under sustained workloads. It is suited for workloads that benefit from multi-threading but do not require continuous, dedicated CPU performance, such as development environments, moderate web serving, and basic database operations. It is less suitable for heavy cryptographic tasks, intensive single-threaded computations, or large-scale LLM inference.
description: The Vultr vc2-6c-16gb is a Cloud Compute virtual server configured with 6 shared vCPUs from an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 320 GB NVMe SSD. It features a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 4 MB L2, and 16 MB L3, and includes one public IPv4 address. Benchmark data shows average multi-core CPU performance (stress-ng score of 6774.42) and solid Redis SET throughput at 6.15 million operations per second, though single-core execution, large-block memory writes, and cryptographic operations are relatively weak. Given its shared CPU architecture, this instance offers a cost-effective resource profile for multi-threaded workloads with variable CPU demands. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, development environments, and moderate web serving rather than sustained, compute-intensive tasks.
